text:
Ireland is prosecuting a man for his signs — I'm going back for his trial 🇮🇪

Hugh Fagan sits on a bench in Wexford with seven homemade signs and his headphones on. The Irish state has charged him with a public order offence. His trial is October 27, and Rebel News has hired him a lawyer.

The Irish government is prosecuting a man for his signs.

His name is Hugh Fagan. He lives in Wexford, a lovely little tourist town in the south-east of Ireland — cobbled streets, coffee shops, a medieval abbey. Most days he walks down to the town square, four blocks from his house, and sits on a bench with seven handmade signs propped up around him.

He wears headphones. He doesn’t shout. He doesn’t hand out leaflets or ask anyone for anything. He isn’t a member of any party. If you want to talk to him, he takes the headphones off and talks to you — and he told me that happens every day. If you don’t, he just sits there.

And for that, a summons came in the post. He’s charged with a public order offence. When I asked him which of the seven signs he was being charged over, he said the police hadn’t told him, that he’d find out in court.

I (@EzraLevant) sat with Hugh in the square this spring, when I was in Ireland for Kirk Loco’s case, and talked to him for 20 minutes.

(It was filmed in May, so when Hugh says his hearing is “next week,” that was an earlier appearance. His trial is now set for Tuesday, October 27.)

Let me tell you how he started.

In May of last year, he was walking past a church near the Tesco on a Sunday. A funeral was coming out, the casket was being put into the hearse, and a beggar was lying across the entrance. Hugh said to himself, enough is enough, and the next week he was in the square with two signs; now, there are seven.

They’re about mass immigration, about churches being burned down across Europe, about the safety of women and children, about the European Union.

I’ll be honest with you: the signs are blunt. I read one of them out loud on camera, and I don’t agree with every word. Where I disagree, it’s with the style more than the substance — I’m worried about mass immigration too, and about what’s happening to women in Ireland. But even if I disagreed with all of it, that’s the point of freedom of speech. It’s the gift you give your opponents if you want it for yourself.

Here’s what gets me.

The Guards — that’s what the Irish call their police — get called on Hugh almost every week. People walk up to him and scream “racist” and “fascist” in his face. The buskers have told him to move. Pro-Palestine activists have told him “nobody wants you here.” Tourists have stood over him waiting for the Guards to come and arrest him. The local paper has written about him twice.

None of those people have been charged with anything. The only person charged is the man sitting quietly on the bench.

Hugh said something to me that stuck. “We’re living in the upside down at the moment,” he said. “What’s true is not true anymore.”

By the way, Hugh told me he’s lived in four countries and never so much as had a parking ticket. He’s not a troublemaker. He’s an unusual man with an unusual way of making his point — I called him the Unreasonable Man, after Bernard Shaw’s line that all progress depends on the unreasonable man, and he liked that.

It reminded me of my friend Chris Elston back in Canada — better known as @BillboardChris — who stands on street corners with a sandwich board. Eccentric, maybe. Criminal? Come on.

This is the pattern in Ireland now, and the more I look at it the more worried I get. Kirk Loco was charged under an anti-terror law for a tweet — for reposting a warning that a migrant had exposed himself to a teenaged girl on a bus. The migrant wasn’t charged; Kirk was. His next hearing is in Bray on October 23, four days before Hugh’s. And now a man with cardboard signs.

The Taoiseach, Ireland's prime minister, goes abroad and calls the country a bastion of free speech. The Irish media cheer the prosecutions on. Nobody in Ireland is pushing back in an organized way.

So we are.

An old friend of mine used to say it’s easier to fight in the first ditch than in the last ditch. Hugh Fagan is the first ditch. If the state can shut up a quiet man with signs in a tourist town, it can shut up anyone. He’s the tripwire. If they get him, they move on to the next one, and the next.

We’ve hired him a proper legal team: Laoise de Brún, a Dublin barrister, and Padraig Langsch, a solicitor. They’re the same lawyers defending Kirk. Their fee for Hugh’s case is €10,000 euros, all in. We’ve already paid half, through the Irish free speech crowdfund you’ve been supporting. The rest is due after the hearing.

And I’ll be in Wexford District Court on October 27, in person, live-tweeting from inside and filming outside. I’ll be in Bray for Kirk four days earlier. One trip, two trials, and you’ll get a report from both courtrooms.

When the Kundalini rises upward, Yoga speaks of five types of vital air: Prana, Apana, Samana, Udana, and Vyana. The kind of Pranayama you are being made to practise—Kapalabhati, whatever form it may be—there are hundreds of types of Pranayama.
Apana Vayu expels the downward discharges below the navel. The Kundalini is located in the sacrum, at the base of the spine, coiled three and a half times, with its tail held in its mouth.This will bring about a universal change. Kundalini exists in every human being, indeed in every living being, in every creature.
When it awakens, the first Bandha is formed at the Muladhara. Then the spine undergoes its own exercise, because all the systems are connected to this point here (at the Sahasrara). Then the navel will draw toward the spine. You cannot make this happen by simply willing it.
Then, as it rises further and passes above the Kanthakupa—the hollow here, below the throat—the third Bandha will be formed. This is called Jalandhara Bandha. Now, beyond this, the spine is short, and there is only a small portion left where all kinds of movement are not possible. So Pranayama takes place.
That Pranayama also happens spontaneously. You will not do it simply by willing it. There are hundreds of types of Pranayama; whichever form is needed will happen on its own. Your inner consciousness will bring it about; it will not be performed by an external Yogacharya.
In this way, as soon as the Kundalini rises above the Ajna Chakra, Samadhi will occur. Without entering Samadhi, the mystery of Nature cannot be known. And the first requirement for Samadhi is complete freedom from disease.
Now even addictions go away. Doctors are greatly surprised, and the West is greatly surprised. They say, ‘Heroin addiction will kill us,’ whereas here, even opium, heroin, and all such addictions are being given up.
That transformation, too, is taking place on a fundamental basis. Creation has arisen from Trigunamayi Maya—the three Gunas: Rajas, Tamas, and Sattva. There are Tamasik tendencies that make demands, and those demands have to be supplied. People who eat meat, drink alcohol, and so on—these Tamasik glands become active and create that demand.
Doctors asked me, ‘Guru Ji, we know that the opium addiction has gone, but what happened to the withdrawal symptoms in someone who had been consuming this poison for twenty years?

Once, Swami Vivekananda Ji was giving a speech in America when an American said, ‘Sir, you are giving such a long lecture, but we are not going to agree with you. In your religion, there are so many restrictions—vegetarianism, non-vegetarianism, and who knows what else. We eat meat and drink alcohol.’ So, right in the middle of his speech, Swami Ji said, ‘You need not give up these things; the things will give you up.’ You do not need to give them up; when they leave you, what will you do then?
How many people give sermons saying, ‘Do not drink alcohol. Do not consume opium.’ Does anyone listen? No one listens. They hear it through one ear and let it out through the other. Why would anyone listen to me? I say, ‘Do not give it up. If you are drinking one bottle, start drinking one and a half from today itself. But do not give up chanting the Name.’ The Name and addiction cannot go together. They cannot coexist. I have helped thousands, even hundreds of thousands, give up their addictions. So, this is the work of transforming the tendency.
In this way, transformation will come through chanting the Name and meditation. This is not some abnormal transformation. This is the evolution that is meant to take place in human beings; it has already begun. The three Koshas (Sheaths) are becoming conscious. Maharshi Aurobindo said that the knowledge attained by our Ancient Sages is returning. We have to give this knowledge to the whole world.
That is why I went to America. I said, ‘I have not come to take your dollars; I have come to donate this knowledge to you.’ Now they are perplexed because their religious identities and ideologies – their isms, come to the forefront—what is Christianity doing, what is Islam doing, what is Judaism doing? I said, ‘Hindus have never accepted the idea of religious conversion. They speak of changing the tendency.’
There is a prophecy: ‘Creation of New World.’ From this very world, new human beings will emerge. ‘Creation of New World’—and what will it be like? They say, ‘Creation of Spiritual World.
Do not tell people the mantra in this way. Tell them that all the other transformations have taken place. And there is nothing surprising about this. This is the Sanjivani Mantra. Start chanting it from now. If there is life in the person, whether it is AIDS, cancer, or hepatitis B, it will be cured—through chanting the Name alone.
Now, several AIDS cases have been cured through meditation on my photograph. But who will highlight this? The government cannot do it. In 2006, several Secretaries of the Government of India came to me in Delhi. They told me, ‘Guru Ji, the work you are doing is based on Hindu Dharma. The Middle East and the West will not allow it to continue. The government will not do it. You continue your work.’
When the Ramayana television serial was made, the Middle East strongly objected to it. But India said, ‘We have already sold the broadcasting rights.’ So I said, ‘I have no problem. Now let me tell you the Name. Just today, someone said this to me. I was told the same thing in Bangalore as well.

There is one syllable: ‘Kleeng,’ the syllable ‘Kleeng.’ In Bangalore too, I was told that many people pronounce it ‘Kleem.’ Do not pronounce it ‘Kleem.’ There is the Hindi vowel ‘a’; as soon as a dot (bindu) is placed above it, what does it become? ‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng’—‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng,’ ‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng,’ ‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng.’

The cycle of coming and going will come to an end; you will be freed from the cycle of birth and death.

text:
Chief Election Commissioner (CIC) of India is an independent constitutional authority. There are demands from a section of people demanding his arrest and prosecution.

Can CIC be arrested for his actions during his term of office in discharge of duties during tenure and or post tenure?

The legal status of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) regarding arrest and prosecution is governed by the Constitution of India and parliamentary statutes.

The short answer is: No, the CEC cannot be arrested or criminally prosecuted for official actions taken in the discharge of duties—neither during tenure nor post-tenure—due to statutory immunity. However, they do not have blanket personal immunity for private/unrelated criminal offenses.

1. Protection for Official Actions (Statutory Immunity)

Under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023:

 * Civil and Criminal Protection: No court can entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceeding against a person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner for any act, thing, or word done, spoken, or purported to be done in the discharge of their official duty or function.

 * Lifelong Scope for Official Duty: Because the statute specifies anyone who "is or was" a Commissioner, this protection extends both during the tenure and post-retirement for actions taken under their official authority.

 * Effect on Arrest: Since courts are barred from taking cognizance or entertaining criminal cases for official conduct, police cannot formally prosecute or seek custody/arrest through judicial process for those official decisions.

2. Personal Criminal Acts (Unrelated to Official Functions)

 * No Constitutional Blanket Immunity: Unlike the President of India and State Governors (who enjoy absolute immunity from criminal proceedings during their term under Article 361 of the Constitution), the CEC has no such personal constitutional shielding.

 * Private Offenses: If a CEC were accused of a regular criminal offense unconnected to the discharge of their official post (e.g., a personal violent crime, personal financial fraud outside official duty), they could theoretically be investigated and arrested under regular criminal procedure. However, even in such cases, arrest of a high constitutional authority typically involves stringent administrative and procedural protocols.

3. Removal from Office (Constitutional Safeguards)

Demands for arrest often arise in political contexts, but the Constitution provides a specific mechanism for accountability rather than criminal arrest:

 * Removal Equivalent to a Supreme Court Judge: Under Article 324(5) of the Constitution, the CEC cannot be removed from office arbitrarily by the executive.

 * They can only be removed through a process akin to impeachment: an order by the President supported by a special majority in both Houses of Parliament (a majority of the total membership and at least two-thirds of the members present and voting) on grounds of proven misbehavior or incapacity.

Current Legal Challenges

The breadth of Section 16 of the 2023 Act has faced significant criticism and legal scrutiny. Public interest petitions (including those filed by civil rights groups like the Association for Democratic Reforms) before the Supreme Court have challenged this provision, arguing that conferring such broad, lifelong immunity from criminal prosecution to an administrative/constitutional body violates Article 14 (Equality before Law) and the basic structure of the Constitution. Unless the Supreme Court strikes down or reads down Section 16, it remains binding law.

Mr. Chandrababu Naidu, why are opposition candidates having to fight for the right to file nominations in Andhra Pradesh?

A candidate reportedly climbing over the wall of a municipal office to submit his nomination. Allegations of nomination papers being snatched and torn. Opposition representatives claiming they were assaulted, detained or prevented from reaching election offices. Police personnel facing serious questions about their conduct.

These are among the disturbing incidents reported during Andhra Pradesh’s local body elections in October 2026.

And this controversy has reached a point where the Supreme Court has had to intervene to protect the electoral process.

What makes the situation particularly serious is that the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission itself has acknowledged that candidates were prevented from filing nominations in four urban local bodies because of intimidation, attacks, torn nomination papers or other adverse circumstances.

When an election authority acknowledges that candidates were obstructed from entering an electoral contest, the government cannot treat the controversy as routine political rivalry.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu owes the people of Andhra Pradesh an explanation.

In Tirupati, YSRCP mayoral candidate Vasu Yadav reportedly climbed over the compound wall of the Municipal Corporation office in an attempt to submit his nomination.

Consider the absurdity of that situation.

A person seeking to participate in an election allegedly could not gain normal access to the very office responsible for receiving nominations.

How did matters reach that point? Who was controlling access to the premises? What assistance did the election officials and police provide?

In Kadapa district, including Proddatur and Pulivendula, opposition candidates complained that nomination documents and party authorisation forms were snatched or torn. Women candidates alleged that restrictions and police action prevented them from reaching nomination centres before the deadline.

In Punganur, clashes involving rival political groups reportedly resulted in injuries and damaged vehicles. YSRCP MP P. V. Midhun Reddy alleged that his convoy was attacked while accompanying candidates. Police accounts described confrontations involving supporters of both parties.

These incidents require investigation based on evidence, not competing political statements.

The videos circulating online should be examined alongside CCTV recordings, police reports, medical records and testimony from those present.

If individuals deliberately destroyed nomination documents, obstructed candidates or used violence to influence the electoral process, their political connections must offer them no protection.

But the most consequential development came from the judiciary.

On 21 October, the Supreme Court considered complaints that opposition candidates had been prevented from submitting nominations and directed the State Election Commission to examine the allegations and provide appropriate safeguards.

Following the Court’s intervention, the Election Commission reopened nominations in four affected urban local bodies on 23 and 24 October.

That decision is an official acknowledgement that the original nomination process had failed to provide a fair opportunity to some candidates.

It does not establish that the ruling party organised every incident. Nor does it determine the criminal responsibility of particular individuals.

But it establishes something the government must confront: serious interference with electoral participation occurred, and corrective action became necessary.

Mr. Naidu, your administration must answer some straightforward questions.

Why were adequate arrangements not in place to ensure that every eligible candidate could submit nomination papers safely?

Were complaints of intimidation brought to the attention of district officials before the nomination deadlines? If so, what preventive measures were taken?

Did police personnel witness the alleged destruction of nomination documents? Were complaints registered promptly, and have the individuals identified in the footage been questioned?

On what grounds were opposition representatives detained or restricted? Were equivalent measures applied to supporters of the ruling coalition where comparable circumstances existed?

Have the relevant CCTV recordings been secured? Will the government support an independent examination of the conduct of police officers and election officials?

And what specific safeguards have now been introduced to ensure that the reopened nomination process is conducted without further interference?

These are not unreasonable demands. They concern the basic functioning of an elected government and the institutions entrusted with conducting elections.

The TDP-led coalition has rejected the YSRCP’s accusations and alleged that opposition supporters themselves contributed to the disturbances.

Those allegations should be investigated with equal seriousness.

Political violence is unacceptable regardless of which party’s supporters are responsible.

However, the government has an obligation that extends beyond defending its own party’s version of events.

The police operate under the authority of the state administration. Public order is the government’s responsibility. Election officials must be able to discharge their duties independently, without pressure from political actors.

The government cannot escape administrative accountability merely by arguing that the opposition also behaved improperly.

Mr. Naidu, you have repeatedly presented yourself as an experienced administrator committed to transforming Andhra Pradesh through investment, infrastructure, technology and economic development.

Those ambitions make the questions surrounding these elections even more important.

Investors may assess a state’s economic prospects through infrastructure, financial policy and business opportunities. Citizens also have a right to assess its governance through the independence of public institutions and the equal application of the law.

A modern administration must be capable of protecting political participation, including the rights of people who oppose the government.

And there is a fundamental difference between defeating an opponent through votes and preventing that opponent from appearing on the ballot.

One is democratic competition.

The other, if deliberately carried out, is an attack on the fairness of the election itself.

A candidate does not need the ruling party’s approval to contest an election. Nor should access to an election office depend on political influence, personal connections or the willingness of local authorities to intervene.

The right to seek election must be protected through lawful procedures, and any restriction must have a legitimate legal basis.

This principle applies equally to TDP, YSRCP, Jana Sena, BJP and every independent candidate.

The Supreme Court’s intervention and the Election Commission’s corrective action must now be followed by transparent investigation and meaningful accountability.

Reopening nominations addresses the immediate problem for some affected candidates. It does not, by itself, answer how the obstruction occurred, whether officials failed in their duties or who should be held responsible.

Those questions cannot be left unresolved once the election schedule moves forward.

Mr. Chandrababu Naidu, the responsibility now rests with your government to demonstrate that the police will protect every candidate, that election officials can act independently and that political influence will not determine who gets to contest.

Publish the findings of the investigations. Explain the actions taken against anyone found responsible. Cooperate fully with the Election Commission and the judiciary. Ensure that candidates from every political party receive equal protection.

And if any public official is found to have deliberately facilitated electoral obstruction, initiate appropriate disciplinary and legal proceedings.

The people of Andhra Pradesh should not have to depend on viral videos, political confrontations and emergency judicial intervention to establish whether candidates are being allowed to file nominations.

An election must be decided by voters at the ballot box, not by whoever controls the entrance to a nomination office.

That is the standard against which the conduct of this government, and every government in India, must be judged.

With early In-Person Absentee Voting starting today (visit the link in the comments for more information. If you are in Germantown, as I am, voting will take place at Village Hall), it’s time once again for my biannual voter guide. As those of you who follow Wisconsin politics know all too well, Wisconsin voters don’t get to take time off. Every election in the state feels like the most important election of our lives. And every election in the state IS the most important election of our lives, at least until the next one… except for maybe this one.

Why? Because, for the first time since 2010, Wisconsin has a chance to move FORWARD once again. The past sixteen years have been difficult. Republicans have decimated the once-famous "Laboratory of Democracy” built by legendary Wisconsin heroes like Fighting Bob LaFollette, and turned it into the Koch Brothers’ playhouse, a place to test their worst, most publicly destructive policies, with the support of vile miscreants like Scott Walker. Walker employed his “divide and conquer” strategy to turn public and private unions against one another (the rich and powerful will do whatever they can to trick the working class into fighting with itself). He planned to systematically dismantle organized labor in Wisconsin at the behest of his billionaire backers who long sought to attack workers’ rights and protections to increase their wealth and power.

The state that birthed “the Wisconsin Idea”, the first state in the union to enshrine workmen’s compensation, the first state to have an unemployment insurance program, the first state to recognize collective bargaining rights for public employees, was now preparing its demise. Beginning with Act 10, right-wing billionaire-puppet Scott Walker ended collective bargaining rights for public employee unions (exempting traditionally conservative unions like Police and sheriff's deputies). Act 10 also made it significantly more difficult to certify and maintain a union, leading to a 29% decrease in public sector union membership rate (46.6% down to a measly 18.5%), and shifted financial burden (retirement and healthcare contributions) onto employees, leading to an exodus of dedicated, talented public servants. Then, four years later, Walker passed “Right to Work”, a classic right-wing misnomer designed to imply the opposite of what it actually does. Like saying the “Patriot Act” (the most invasive, expansive, and unconstitutional advancement of mass surveillance in history) was meant to expand freedom when, in reality, it massively infringes on personal privacy rights and constitutional protections. “Right to Work” is touted as a way to increase worker freedom and choice when, in reality, it significantly weakens workers' bargaining power.

Scott Walker and his billionaire buddies did everything they could to weaken worker power in the state, and they succeeded. And I haven’t even touched on his attacks on the environment, consumer protections, disability rights, immigrant rights, local control, public schools, elections, women’s health, nor his massive corporate tax cuts. And don’t get me started on the secrecy agreements Republican lawmakers signed so that Scott Walker could sign aggressively gerrymandered maps, considered the worst in the nation after receiving an “F” from the Princeton Gerrymandering Project. Since 2011, Wisconsin has experienced a dramatic increase in child poverty rates, nonexistent wage growth, steep cuts to K-through-12 public schools and the state university system, and a significant decline in water quality, per Dan Kaufman, author of “The Fall of Wisconsin: The Conservative Conquest of a Progressive Bastion and the Future of American Politics”. Under Republican leadership, Wisconsin has fallen backward. Scott Walker is a sleazebag. His legacy reflects that.

But all of that can change come November. We have a chance to flip the Wisconsin Legislature and, when we do, Wisconsin will reclaim its mantle as the most “Forward”-thinking state in the country. The Legislature alone isn’t enough, however. We also have to retain the Governor’s Mansion. When we secure the Trifecta, we will signal to the nation that Wisconsin is restoring our progressive roots, reclaiming our progressive history, and redefining our progressive future. As goes Wisconsin, so goes the nation.
Here I will lay out WHAT decisions I have made and WHY I feel each choice is best. Election day, Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026, is two weeks away. Our vote is our voice, and we all deserve to be heard! Talk to your friends, family, neighbors, etc. and MAKE SURE everyone has a plan to vote. Early voting is incredibly easy, I highly suggest it if election day does not work for your schedule.

This guide will be in the order of each race on my ballot, covering only races I have on my ballot. To see an example of what your ballot will look like, visit myvote.wi (.gov) and click “What’s On My Ballot”.
Starting from the top of (my) ballot, we begin with…
—----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
𝙂𝙤𝙫𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙤𝙧 / 𝙇𝙞𝙚𝙪𝙩𝙚𝙣𝙖𝙣𝙩 𝙂𝙤𝙫𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙤𝙧- 𝘿𝙖𝙫𝙞𝙙 𝘾𝙧𝙤𝙬𝙡𝙚𝙮/𝙎𝙖𝙧𝙖𝙝 𝙂𝙤𝙙𝙡𝙚𝙬𝙨𝙠𝙞

Those who know me, and have followed my content, are very well aware of my stance in the Gubernatorial Primary. While the results did not go the way that I had hoped, the democratic process is sacrosanct. But, friends, we still have a damn good choice here. I won’t get everything I wanted from Governor @DavidCCrowley, but I will get most of what I wanted. More importantly, I’m getting a Governor who will listen to his constituents and understands the importance of compromise. A Governor that will fight for working-class people instead of his three billionaire donors. A Governor that we can work with (and pressure when necessary) to enact the desperately necessary progressive policies this state hungers for. As he has done throughout his career. In particular, David’s support for $20 for ‘26, a Living Wage for Wisconsin is of immense importance to me. All work has value, all labor has dignity, all Wisconsinites deserve a living wage. We can put money in the pockets of 800,000 working Wisconsinites, helping families put a roof over their heads, food on their tables, and maybe a nice trip to the Dells now and then, or a weekend at the Zoo or the movies, time permitting. The working-class is struggling. The rich are getting richer, the rest of us are falling further and further behind. This is an opportunity to tangibly improve the lives of 1 out of 5 working Wisconsinites. Money that will go right back into our communities (instead of being sent to some overseas Cayman Islands account) to grow Wisconsin’s economy. Wages are a policy choice, wages represent leverage. For too long, the boss class has abused and exploited the working class, hollowing out the middle class as they siphoned TRILLIONS of dollars into the pockets of an elite few. That ends come November. Which is why I will be voting for David Crowley.

Tom Tiffany, of course, is a uniquely atrocious candidate as he has a long history of voting against the best interests of both Wisconsin and democracy at large. Let’s not forget, Tiffany voted to decertify the 2020 election, attempting to throw away the votes of 3.3 million Wisconsinites. As I said above, the democratic process is sacrosanct. Tom Tiffany is an election denier who tried to invalidate the will of Wisconsin. That is unforgivable. Not to mention, he refused to sign the Epstein Files Discharge Petition in an effort to protect Donald Trump. Tom Tiffany is another Trump lackey who will do everything he can to avoid offending Donald Trump, regardless of how it impacts the people of Wisconsin. His voting record on environmental issues is one of the worst in the nation, read up on his track record of prioritizing mining corporations/interests over preserving Wisconsin’s natural resources if you don’t believe me. And, oh yeah, 93% of his campaign funds have come from three billionaires. Bought-and-sold Tom Tiffany is following in the footsteps of Scott Walker (even using the same three billionaires). I don’t vote for election-denying pedophile-protectors, so I will never consider Toxic Tom Tiffany.
—----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
𝘼𝙩𝙩𝙤𝙧𝙣𝙚𝙮 𝙂𝙚𝙣𝙚𝙧𝙖𝙡- 𝙅𝙤𝙨𝙝 𝙆𝙖𝙪𝙡

Attorney General doesn’t get the coverage of the bigger, sexier races… but the head of the Wisconsin Department of Justice does serve a prominent role in public safety as the chief legal officer for the state. While, like a good offensive lineman, most won’t hear your name if you’re doing your job well, @JoshKaulwi has taken on (and won) some tough battles. I would like to see him go after the Trump Administration harder, but he DID successfully defend the 2020 Presidential election when Wisconsin Republicans (like Tom Tiffany) tried to dismiss our votes. He also joined the challenge to a U.S. Postal Service rule designed to undermine mail-in voting, sued to stop Elon Musk’s blatantly illegal election bribery, defended women’s health decisions by obtaining a Wisconsin Supreme Court ruling making it CLEAR that abortions are not broadly banned in Wisconsin, and secured a MAJOR antitrust victory against John Deere. For those unfamiliar, look into “Right to Repair”, this precedent is HUGE for all consumers, but especially farmers, across Wisconsin. Josh has a track record of taking on the powerful to support the people of Wisconsin, and I’m excited to vote for him to continue doing so.
—----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
𝙎𝙚𝙘𝙧𝙚𝙩𝙖𝙧𝙮 𝙤𝙛 𝙎𝙩𝙖𝙩𝙚- 𝙅𝙤𝘾𝙖𝙨𝙩𝙖 𝙕𝙖𝙢𝙖𝙧𝙧𝙞𝙥𝙖

A working class-champion top to bottom, JoCasta Zamarripa for WI Secretary of State is a public servant and community leader with years of experience fighting for working people. Despite being groundbreaking, in more ways than one, she has been at the forefront of multiple major Milwaukee efforts, including being the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan (Growing MKE). Affordable housing is a crisis throughout Wisconsin, and I applaud leaders like JoCasta for taking on this challenge. Her focus on funding for schools (so communities don’t have to go to referenda every year), housing relief for working people, and affordable child care highlight a candidate who understands the issues impacting the people of Wisconsin and has a vision to help alleviate some of those most pressing concerns.
—----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
𝙎𝙩𝙖𝙩𝙚 𝙏𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙨𝙪𝙧𝙚𝙧- 𝙔𝙚𝙚 𝙇𝙚𝙣𝙜 𝙓𝙞𝙤𝙣𝙜

@Yeefowi is an absolute treasure, and as an OWR-endorsed candidate, this choice is about as easy as it gets. With extensive experience serving as a County Supervisor, School Board Treasurer, and former Village Trustee, Yee understands public budgets and the importance of judicious decisions with taxpayer dollars on the line. With a plan to oversee, protect, and grow the Common School Fund, push for transparency, accountability, and responsible management of public funds, and steward public lands responsibly, Yee is ready to use this office for public good, despite the State Legislature stripping its powers over the past few decades (by both parties). Yee has my enthusiastic support!
—----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Andy Beck for Wisconsin is a political newcomer, a breath of fresh air in a district that is rotting beneath the stench of do-nothing Scott Fitzgerald. A working-class man from a union household, Andy is a common-sense candidate focused on protecting the pillars of American democracy, rights, and freedoms. I often joke that 90% of solidarity is showing up, and Andy ALWAYS shows up. He’s one of the few people I know who attends more events than I do!

Career politician Scott Fitzgerald, on the other hand, never shows up. He never shows up for his constituents, he never shows up for Wisconsin, he never shows up for America. In fact, the last time he held a public event (February of 2025), it made national news when hundreds of constituents in WEST BEND showed up to express frustrations, only to have Scott condescendingly defend the egregious behavior of Elon Musk and his little DOGE team. GOBI WAS BOUGHT IN 2009. HE HAS BEEN DELIVERING EVER SINCE.

Let’s stop pretending, Gobi. You are not a strongman, a fakir, or a man sent by God. You are a purchase. In January 2009, at Vibrant Gujarat, India’s richest men stood on a stage and called you a king among kings, a man fit to lead the nation, before your own party had decided anything. Nobody crowns a stranger. They crown an investment.

Then they packaged you: the tea-seller story, the 56-inch chest, the costume changes, the laser shows, the stadium entrances, and reportedly an American lobbying firm to polish the shine. A real leader is formed by struggle. You were formed by marketing, and it shows every time you step in front of a camera without a script.

Then they paid. Thousands of crores in anonymous electoral bonds, about half of all of it into your party’s account, until the Supreme Court tore the scheme up as unconstitutional in February 2024. Honest money doesn’t hide its name. Yours hid behind a law you wrote for it.

Then you delivered. Airports, ports, coal, power, highways, the commanding heights of the economy, handed over one at a time to the same few names. When America indicted Gautam Adani over an alleged bribery scheme, you stood beside Trump and called it a “personal matter”. You have an opinion on India’s plates, wardrobes and marriages, and you suddenly discover privacy when your friend is charged.

Your courage is a one-way street, and it only ever points down. You tear-gas students, beat girls at protests, jail comedians, lift the Leader of the Opposition into a police bus, and send the khaki after teenagers who wave the flag. Then Trump announces your ceasefire before you do, claims credit for it dozens of times, slaps 50% tariffs on Indian goods, and the great lion of Delhi cannot say his name. Fifty-six inches for Indian students, a folded hand for Washington.

In twelve years you have not faced a single open press conference in India. A monk takes questions, a leader takes questions, a schoolteacher takes questions. Only a product is afraid of them, because one honest question is enough to crack the plastic. So you talk to the nation once a month on the radio, alone, and call your monologue a conversation.

You wore your own name on your suit to meet Obama, and a diamond merchant bought it for ₹4.31 crore. In 2024 you told India you were not born biologically. That was the most honest thing you have ever said, because nobody is born like you. You were assembled in a boardroom, to order, with a warranty card issued to two families.

Now look at the man you fear. Rahul Gandhi refused ministries, resigned when he lost, walked four thousand kilometres on a broken knee, sat through fifty hours of your ED, lost his seat and his house, and still named A1 and A2 to your face in Parliament. Nobody bought him, which is why he can look you in the eye. You have never been able to return the look, because a purchased man can only look at his owners or at the floor.

A parasite feeds on a host, gives nothing back, and calls the host’s weakness its own strength. The host is India. You feed on its savings, its institutions, its young and its vote, and you call the bleeding “Amrit Kaal”.

The next time someone tells you Gobi is a strong leader, ask them who he has ever stood up to who was stronger than him. Wait for the name. There isn’t one. Then send them this.

1)The FDA Should Grant Americans the Right to Try New Cancer Treatments
A Commentary By Stephen Moore

Tuesday, October 20, 2026
Every few months, a young 19-year-old woman from South Carolina boards a plane to London. She isn't going sightseeing. She's going to get her next dose of a cancer treatment that was invented in the United States, developed by an American company, and credited by her doctors with clearing a brain tumor other surgeons had refused to touch.
   She was diagnosed with glioblastoma at 16. It is the most common and most lethal brain cancer, the disease that killed John McCain and Beau Biden. Her tumor came back so aggressively after her first surgery that doctors stopped operating. This was a death sentence.
   But one surgeon at the University of California, Los Angeles, agreed to perform the invasive surgery.
   Afterward she began a personalized immunotherapy made from her own tumor tissue and her own immune cells. Today her scans are clear, and she's in college.
   Her family has health insurance, but they must pay for every flight and every dose out of pocket, with help from money raised from strangers online through GoFundMe.
   Why London? Because in Britain, a licensed physician can prescribe a promising treatment that for no rational reason has not been approved even on a limited and trial basis in the U.S.
   Today there are dozens of promising drugs and therapies for multiple forms of horrific and crippling diseases: cancer, Alzheimer's, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's and diabetes, to name a few. Patients are literally dying waiting for the chance to use these treatments on an experimental basis. At the very bare minimum, they give suffering patients hope. But not in America.
   So much for "my body, my choice."
   But why not let the patient, not Food and Drug Administration regulators, decide the most important decision of her life: how to stay alive?
   This is a cruel way for America to make health treatment decisions. I have no idea whether this particular cancer treatment really works, but in the case of a deadly disease, why not let patients try whatever alternative treatments they want? Isn't it sad that in the land of the free, individuals have fewer treatment choices than most other nations in the world?
   By taking an experimental drug or treatment, these disease sufferers are being thrown a potential lifeline while also advancing the medical discovery process by acting as test cases. This is doing future patients a favor.
   President Donald Trump has signed "right to try" laws, but the FDA remains an impediment. The waiting times to get approved are long, which means the tumors in millions of patients get larger. The risk-averse FDA seems wedded to its old way of doing business, with interminable testing in clinical trials while patients die waiting.
   There are three steps the FDA and the White House can take to help expand right-to-try and avoid often-fatal bureaucratic delays.
   First, for rare diseases, adopt a test of "plausible success." If there is compelling evidence that a treatment COULD work, let patients try it.
   Second, expand "compassionate use." A physician treating a patient with a terminal diagnosis should be able to prescribe a promising investigational therapy with the patient's informed consent. The doctor would notify the FDA rather than ask its permission and drown in paperwork.
   Third, if a drug or treatment is approved in a developed nation, allow patients in the U.S. to use it with a different designation than "FDA approved." This leaves the decision of whether to try the drug up to the patient, not the bureaucrat.
   Sometimes in medicine, the best and often most unexpected results come from the trial-and-error process.
   It's a sad and cruel development that Europeans and South Americans can gain access to the latest breakthroughs in medicines while Americans can't. Rich families can afford the costs of flying across the world to receive these treatments, but middle-class and poor families often can't.
   What makes this predicament doubly foolish and inhumane is that many of these experimental treatments were developed in America.
   The Trump administration has an opportunity to show that "Make America Healthy Again" means letting American patients use American breakthroughs at home. The pathway has been announced. The president has already shown he cares about patients like this young woman. Now the FDA and Department of Health and Human Services have to deliver.
   No American should have to buy a plane ticket to London to get an American cure.
   Stephen Moore is a former Trump senior economic adviser and the cofounder of Unleash Prosperity, which advocates for education freedom for all children.

Stephen Moore (born February 16, 1960) is an American economist, writer, and conservative television commentator. He co-founded and served as president of the Club for Growth from 1999 to 2004. Moore is a former member of The Wall Street Journal editorial board. He worked at The Heritage Foundation from 1983 to 1987 and again since 2014. Moore advocates tax cuts and other supply-side policies. His columns have appeared in The Wall Street Journal, The Washington Times, The Weekly Standard, and National Review.Moore advised the presidential campaigns of Herman Cain in 2012 and Donald Trump in 2016. Along with Larry Kudlow, Moore advised the Trump administration during the writing and passage of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017. Amid bipartisan resistance in spring 2019, Moore withdrew his name from consideration to serve on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.

Education
Moore grew up in New Trier Township, Illinois. He attended Saints Faith Hope & Charity School in Winnetka and graduated from New Trier High School in 1978.[1] He received a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) from the University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign and a Master of Arts (M.A.) in economics from George Mason University.[2]

Career
From 1983 to 1987, Moore served as the Grover M. Hermann Fellow in Budgetary Affairs at The Heritage Foundation. In 1987, Moore was the research director of President Ronald Reagan's Privatization Commission.[3] Moore spent ten years as a fellow of the Cato Institute, a libertarian think tank.[4][5] As senior economist of the U.S. Congress Joint Economic Committee under Chairman Dick Armey of Texas, Moore was said to be "instrumental in creating the FairTax proposal".[4]In 1999, Moore co-founded and became president of the Club for Growth, a group advocating tax cuts and a reduction in government spending, along with supporting political candidates who favored free-market economic policies.[6] While president of the group, Moore targeted "Republicans in Name Only" whom he viewed as not aligned with his anti-tax views; he criticized Republican Senators who did not readily embrace tax cuts, including Arlen Specter, Olympia Snowe, and George Voinovich.[7]At the Club for Growth, Moore sought to change the Republican Party, saying in 2003, "We want to take over the party's fundraising. We want it to be, in 10 years, that no one can win a Senate or a House seat without the support of the Club for Growth."[7] From 2003 to 2004, the Club for Growth was the single largest fundraiser for Republican House and Senate candidates, being outdone only by the Republican party itself.[6]In December 2004, the Club for Growth's board voted to remove Moore as president, with his opponents within the organization upset by his criticism of President George Bush and by the narrow defeat of Senator Pat Toomey, who had the group's support. After Moore's departure, lawyers for the group sent letters to him and members of his new organization, the Free Enterprise Fund, threatening legal action for allegedly stealing the group's mailing list to raise funds for his new organization; Moore's partner Mallory Factor stated the list was acquired elsewhere.[8]After he left the Club for Growth, Moore founded the 501(c)(4) Free Enterprise Fund with other former Club for Growth members including Arthur Laffer and Mallory Factor.[9] In 2005, Moore left the Free Enterprise Fund to serve on the editorial board of the Wall Street Journal.[5]On September 19, 2005, the Federal Election Commission (FEC) filed suit against the Club For Growth, alleging that the group had failed to register as a political action committee in the 2000, 2002, and 2004 election cycles "despite spending millions of dollars on federal campaign activity during the 2000, 2002, and 2004 election cycle." In 2007, the FEC and the Club for Growth agreed to settle the lawsuit, paying $350,000.[10]Moore was involved with the consulting firms Arduin, Laffer & Moore Econometrics,[11] and 32 Advisors.[12] In May 2015, Moore co-founded the advocacy group Committee to Unleash Prosperity with Laffer, Larry Kudlow, and Steve Forbes.[13]Moore advised Herman Cain, a former presidential candidate and business executive, on his 9-9-9 Tax Plan for his 2012 presidential campaign.[14]In 2014, The Heritage Foundation announced that Moore would rejoin the think tank as chief economist.[15] Since March 2015 his profile on the Heritage website has described him as a "Distinguished Visiting Fellow."[16][17]In 2017, Moore worked with Larry Kudlow on overhauling the US tax policy for the Trump administration, which was eventually passed into law by Congress.[18]In 2017, he left Fox News Channel to join CNN as a senior economic analyst, leaving that position in early 2019.[19][20]In 2025, he left The Heritage Foundation.[21]

Writings and statements
In July 2008, as the Fed had for months been rapidly cutting interest rates as the economy weakened into what became the Great Recession, Moore stated, "I happen to believe we should be raising rates, not cutting them."[22][23]Moore supports abolishing the income tax, and replacing it with a national sales tax.[24][25]Moore rejects the scientific consensus on climate change. In 2009, he described climate change as "the biggest scam of the last two decades".[26] In columns and op-eds, Moore called those with concerns about climate change "Stalinistic" and has accused climate scientists of being part of a global conspiracy to obtain money via research grants.[27][28] In an April 2019 interview, Moore said that the Federal Reserve should not consider the economic impacts of climate change in decision-making. "The Fed's job is to keep prices stable; that's all it is," he said. "It's not to get involved in political and policy issues."[29]Moore wrote a 2014 Kansas City Star opinion piece entitled, "What's the matter with Paul Krugman?," responding to Krugman's earlier opinion piece "Charlatans, Cranks and Kansas", which had discussed a recent major tax cut in Kansas.[30][31] Moore said that job creation had been superior in low-taxation states during the five years ending June 2009 following the recession. After errors were found in Moore's data, he sought to correct the errors with different data that were also incorrect. Miriam Pepper, editorial page editor for the Star stated "I won't be running anything else from Stephen Moore." Moore acknowledged his error in an email that also said, "My point is that they don't change the conclusion that the no income tax states have substantially outperformed the high income tax states over every period since about 1970…."[32][33]In a 2014 op-ed in The Washington Times, Moore cited the role of a "culture of virtue" in America's economic success, writing, "What is irrefutable is that marriage with a devoted husband and wife in the home is a far better social program than food stamps, Medicaid, public housing or even all of them combined."[34][35]Moore has often expressed support for some variation of a gold standard. In 2015, he declared, "We have got to get rid of the Federal Reserve and move towards a gold standard in this country!" Few economists support a gold standard.[36][37][38]During a 2016 debate on the minimum wage, Moore stated, "I'm a radical on this. I'd get rid of a lot of these child labor laws. I want people starting to work at 11, 12."[39]In 2018, Moore and Laffer wrote the book Trumponomics, in which they lauded the Trump administration's economic policies[18][40] and criticized the economic performance of the George W. Bush years.[41] Trump endorsed the book in a March 2019 tweet.[42] In the book, Moore and Laffer argue that the Trump administration's 2017 tax plan would raise GDP growth rates to as much as 6% and not increase budget deficits.[40] In a 2019 review of the book, conservative N. Gregory Mankiw, an economics professor at Harvard University and head of the Council of Economic Advisors under President George W. Bush, described the book as "snake-oil economics", writing that Moore and Laffer's analysis was based on "wishful thinking" rather than "the foundation of professional consensus or serious studies from peer-reviewed journals".[40][43]Moore asserted in a December 2018 appearance on CNN that the Federal Reserve was causing deflation in the economy, although Commerce Department data showed there was consistent inflation.[44][45][46] In April 2019, Moore asserted deflation was "the whole reason the economy was so poor in late 2018", although inflation was 2.2% in the fourth quarter of 2018.[47][46]In September 2018, Moore wrote a Wall Street Journal opinion piece entitled, "The Corporate Tax Cut Is Paying for Itself," in which he asserted that "faster-than-expected growth has produced a revenue windfall," when comparing "the August 2018 economic forecast from the Congressional Budget Office with the one from June 2017, before the tax cuts passed." Corporate tax receipts for the fiscal year ended September 2018 were down 31% from the prior fiscal year, the largest decline since records began in 1934, except for during the Great Recession when corporate profits, and hence corporate tax receipts, plummeted.[48][49][50][51]In February 2019, Moore stated, "There's no bigger swamp in Washington than the Federal Reserve Board. It's filled with hundreds of economists who are worthless, who have the wrong model in their mind. They should all be, they should all be fired and they should be replaced by good economists."[52]Before his nomination to the Federal Reserve Board, in late December 2018 Moore stated, while on a radio talk show, that he believed "the people on the Federal Reserve Board should be thrown out for economic malpractice".[14]On March 13, 2019, Moore co-authored a column in the Wall Street Journal which asserted that the Federal Reserve's policies were slowing the economy and causing "wild swings in the stock market", at a time when the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 13% for the year. He also asserted that the Fed should focus more on commodity price changes rather than overall price changes. Larry Kudlow, the Director of the U.S. National Economic Council, showed the article to President Trump, who decided he wanted to place Moore on the Federal Reserve Board.[14][44]Moore called for higher interest rates when the economy was recovering from the Great Recession under Barack Obama, but has called for lower rates when the economy has fully recovered and continues to grow under Donald Trump.[38] Moore stated in August 2018, "I have to confess: I was wrong about inflation in 2009 and 2010. I thought there would be a lot of inflation with the Fed lowering rates to practically zero, and that was wrong."[53]In April 2020, Moore referred to individuals who protested stay-at-home orders during the coronavirus pandemic as "the modern-day Rosa Parks — they are protesting against injustice and a loss of liberties."[54] He ran a group named Save Our Country, which argued for the reopening of the economy amid the coronavirus pandemic.[55] Moore argued against coronavirus relief in the form of unemployment benefits, arguing that "giving people money" was not an economic stimulus.[56] Moore said, if it were true that it was the stimulus, "we could just give everybody $100,000 and we'd all be rich right? It's just so stupid."[56]In 2023, Moore co-authored the chapter on the Department of the Treasury in the Heritage Foundation's Project 2025 book, Mandate for Leadership: The Conservative Promise.[57][58]

Unsuccessful nomination to Federal Reserve Board

Nomination
On March 22, 2019, Trump announced he would nominate Moore to fill one of the two vacant seats at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.[59][14] After the nomination was announced, Moore stated "I'm kind of new to this game, frankly, so I'm going to be on a steep learning curve myself about how the Fed operates, how the Federal Reserve makes it decisions, and this is a real, exciting opportunity for me."[60]
Reactions
Democratic Senators denounced Moore as unqualified for the post, and called upon Trump to drop the nomination.[61][62] Democrats also criticized Moore over an unpaid $75,000 tax lien entered against him.[62] Though some key Republican senators expressed support for Moore's nomination, including members of the Senate Banking Committee, enough Republican senators voiced concerns about Moore to place his confirmation in jeopardy.[61][63] Republican senator Richard Shelby said, "I've always said they could use diversity, you don't need to be a Nobel laureate or University of Chicago professor."[64]The nomination stirred immediate criticism by economists,[65][66][14][67] and was widely viewed as the most political appointment to the Federal Reserve Board since the 1980s.[44][68] Benn Steil, director of international economics for the Council on Foreign Relations, stated he found the decision appalling.[69] Monetary economist George Selgin stated he believed Moore was unfit to serve on the Board.[66] Economist Justin Wolfers called the selection of Moore "the first genuinely bad Trump pick for the Fed" and called on the Senate not to confirm Moore.[44] Harvard economics professor Greg Mankiw said that Moore "does not have the intellectual gravitas" for the position.[70][71] Economist Menzie Chinn noted that Moore has not authored or co-authored any peer-reviewed journal articles.[72]In April 2019, 105 professors, former government officials, and analysts signed a one-sentence letter expressing support for Moore's candidacy for the Federal Reserve Board. Signatories included Steve Forbes, Ed Feulner, and Bill Ford, the former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.[73] Endorsements for Moore's nomination also came from his long-time collaborator Larry Kudlow, who recommended the appointment,[44] and from Adam Brandon, president of the conservative advocacy group FreedomWorks.[67] Moore's former employer, The Wall Street Journal editorial board, endorsed Moore for the Fed on March 28, 2019.[74] In an appearance on Fox Business Network, political commentator Charlie Gasparino described Steve Moore as "the counterweight to [Chair of the Federal Reserve Jerome] Powell's hawkishness."[75] Journalist Fred Barnes defended Moore as "a disrupter, like Trump."[76]In April 2019, CNN and The New York Times reported on several articles Moore had written in the National Review in the early 2000s that disparaged women, which Moore dismissed as spoofs or jokes. The Times reported, "Congressional Republicans say [Moore's views on interest rates and the gold standard] are less likely to impede Mr. Moore's confirmation prospects than concerns over his personal life and past statements."[77][78]Moore's call on the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates was also controversial. Lowering interest rates was supported by Trump but opposed by Fed chairman Powell and other policymakers at the time.[79] The Federal Reserve later lowered rates by a quarter of a percent in September 2019 and again the next month. Moore reacted by calling it "an example of where I was right, and where my critics were wrong."[80]
Withdrawal and aftermath
On May 2, 2019, Moore withdrew his name from consideration, saying "The unrelenting attacks on my character have become untenable for me and my family and 3 more months of this would be too hard on us." Following his withdrawal, Moore penned an op-ed in the Wall Street Journal where he decried his critics, writing, "What did me in was not my economic ideas but gutter campaign tactics and personal assaults."[81] Senate Republicans expressed relief that Moore's withdrawal meant that they would not have to cast a vote on his nomination.[82]After his nomination was withdrawn, Moore returned to his previous positions with FreedomWorks, The Heritage Foundation, and Committee to Unleash Prosperity. Additionally, Moore became chief economic officer of Frax, a cryptocurrency company that branded itself "the world's decentralized central bank".[83]

Personal life
Moore was married to Allison Moore until 2011.[71] In 2012, a Virginia court held Moore in contempt of court for failing to pay his ex-wife $300,000 in spousal support, child support, and other obligations in his divorce settlement.[71] Moore did not respond to repeated court requests to make payments and failed to appear for a deposition before the court threatened to have him arrested and ordered him to sell his home to make the payments; the court revoked the order at Moore's request after he made a $217,000 payment.[84][34] In January 2018, the IRS obtained a tax lien against Moore for $75,328 in unpaid federal taxes, interest, and penalties, alleging Moore had filed a "fraudulent" tax return in 2014. Moore stated that his accountant made an error in improperly deducting child support payments and that the lien was the result of an IRS miscalculation,[62] though Moore says he paid the lien and Montgomery County, Maryland Circuit Court records show the case is closed.[85] In addition to the child support payments, the IRS also disallowed other deductions Moore had claimed.[84]Moore has three sons[86] and, as of 2019, is married to Anne Carey.[87]

MeitY's advisory to Meta directs the suppression of protest reporting on Instagram and Facebook. It must be withdrawn.

19 Oct 2026

On 10 October 2026, the Cyber Laws Division of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued an advisory to Meta Platforms bearing File No. 6(2)/2026-Cyberlaws. It was not published on the MEITY website and first HT and then PTI reported it on 18 October. Any such advisory is not a legal order and MEITY is not legally empowered to issue them on the basis of any statutory provision. This advisory followed, by two days, an advisory of 8 October to all social media intermediaries calling for "enhanced diligence" over content on "ongoing public events", asking platforms to "label or add context" to misleading content and to "give priority to complaints from authorised Government agencies".  IFF called for the withdrawal of that advisory on 9 October. The Meta advisory was issued on the day the Delhi Police detained protesters and journalists at the demonstrations called over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

The advisory states that content relating to "public-order and law and order situations" is being "prominently displayed and recommended" on Meta's platforms and, "when presented without adequate context or disproportionately amplified", "may contribute to public confusion, apprehension and disturbance of public order and social tranquillity". It singles out "unverified or misleading claims regarding the imposition of emergency, restrictions, police action or other official measures". Further, Meta is advised to review its "recommendation and content ranking mechanisms", to ensure its systems "do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives", and to furnish "information or assistance" to law enforcement, "with immediate effect". PTI reports that the Ministry acted on inputs from "agencies" that Meta's platforms were not promoting all "narratives" equally.

This advisory matches restrictions on META platforms related to protest content and reporting in the same timline. On 10 October, the Instagram account of Molitics India was withheld in India. On 11 October, a Mathrubhumi English reel showing a woman clinging to a pole as police officers attempted to detain her was restricted citing, "a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement", and a video report by Observer Post Hindi was restricted on Facebook by what Meta called an "automated system" acting under the IT Rules, 2021. On 12 October, the Instagram account of journalist Shubhangi Das Gupta was restricted in India for alleged non-compliance with "local IT Rules". On 13 October, the account of Journo Mirror (about five lakh followers) was withheld. The account of Fridays For Future India has since been withheld without any stated reason. Meta's notices to these users do not disclose what is unlawful about the content. 

As per notices shared by us by those who have been censored by META, they take two forms: 

1. "a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement under Section 79(3)(b)", and, 

2. "through an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements under India's Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules". 

Neither names the issuing agency, the order, the provision of law or offence the content is said to disclose, or the URL complained of. We know due to litigation that the first notice related to a Sahyog order issued by a Law Enforcement Agency (LEA), while the second one is without any legal order. At the same time, several users received no communication at all. Instagram used the same "automated system" notice against Anjali Priya, Varnika Dhawan and Sachin Gupta after the July protests, and against cartoonist Satish Acharya, who lost nine cartoons and then his account between February and September 2026. 

In April 2026, The Hindu reported that Meta automatically restricts government and police flagged content in India at scale, and seeks a separate government direction before restoring content later found to be legally unsupported. IFF objected to Meta on 4 May 2026. IFF condemns the advisory of 10 October and the restrictions imposed in its wake. An executive communication that instructs a platform to suppress "unverified" claims about "police action" and to correct a "limited set of narratives", issued on the day of a police crackdown and kept from the public, is a censorship directive in all but name.  It makes the State the editor of what Indians may see of a protest against the State. IFF calls upon MeitY to withdraw it and upon Meta to disclose what it has done under it.

Our demands

1. MeitY must withdraw the advisories of 8 and 10 October 2026 forthwith and publish them.

2. MeitY must abandon proposed Rule 3(4) and restrict content only by reasoned, published orders under Section 69A or notices compliant with Rule 3(1)(d).

3. Meta must disclose every takedown, account restriction and act of downranking carried out under the advisories, and its compliance report to the Ministry.

4. Meta must restore the accounts and posts of journalists, outlets and creators restricted since 8 October 2026 unless it holds a valid legal order, and must furnish that order to the person affected.

5. Meta must suspend the automated restriction of content in India and disclose on what inputs its "automated system" acts.

Any person whose account or content has been withheld in India since 8 October 2026 may write to IFF at legal@internetfreedom.in. IFF is providing assistance pro bono.

'Jurisprudence in India today appears to be governed by four made-in-India/swadeshi doctrines which should be a blot on any justice system: fait accompli, sealed cover, ignore the science, and reward the criminal. Importantly, even constitutional challenges to the executive’s actions are kept on the backburner for so long (Article 370, CAA, SIR, Shiv Sena split) that by the time they are decided, it is impossible to turn back the clock and undo what the government of the day has already implemented on the ground.
The sealed cover has become the standard fallback option for denying full disclosure to civil society petitioners, or for not giving rebuttable reasons for a particular judgment (Rafale, Pegasus, Vantara, Hindenburg). Increasingly, this spectre of our swadeshi jurisprudence, like the executive, shows disdain and contempt for science, as in the case of stray dogs, Aravalli mountains, the Char Dham highway, and the Great Nicobar project. More trust is reposed on government-appointed committees and patently partisan ministries than on scientists, domain experts and specialised organisations working in the relevant field. Finally, this mutant form of justice also ensures that the criminal will be duly allowed to keep the proceeds of his crime (Ram Mandir theft, electoral bonds) even as his actions are declared irregular! A judicial paraprosdokian if ever there was one.'

Delhi High Court has directed domain name registrars to stop offering privacy protection as a default feature and to implement KYC verification for all domain registrations in India.

Fraudsters had been registering websites using names of companies like Tata Sky, Dabur, Amul and Bajaj Finance to offer fake jobs, franchises and dealerships, collecting crores from unsuspecting victims.

The Court found that registrars were collecting virtually no verifiable information from those registering domains. 

In one case, a fraudster had used Dabur's own office address to register a fake Dabur domain. Not a single legitimate registrant came forward to claim rights over any of the 1100 domain names during three years of litigation.

Justice Prathiba directed that registrant details must be disclosed to trademark owners and law enforcement within 72 hours of a request. Fraudulent domain names cannot be put back in the common pool after expiry. Registrars promoting alternative domains containing protected trademarks will lose safe harbour protection.

The Court also noted that some foreign registrars like Namecheap had initially refused to comply with Indian court orders, relenting only after their services were blocked in India. The judgment makes clear that registrars who repeatedly defy Indian courts may face similar blocking under Section 69A of the IT Act.

These actions often happen under two parallel mechanisms of India’s Information Technology Act, 2000.

First, under Section 69A, which allows the government to issue blocking orders on broad grounds such as national security or public order. Read with Rule 16 of the Information Technology (Procedure and Safeguards for Blocking Access of Information by Public) Rules, 2009, this provision requires confidentiality regarding all requests and complaints received, as well as actions taken.

Second, Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, 2000, allows authorities to pressure platforms to remove content by threatening loss of “safe harbour” protections if platforms fail to comply with government or court directions. In practice, this creates strong incentives for platforms to over-comply.

India, Brazil and South Africa conclude IBSAMAR IX

The ninth edition of IBSAMAR, the trilateral naval exercise of India, Brazil and South Africa, concluded at Naval Base Simon's Town on October 20. Held under the theme "Stronger Together Towards a Shared Future in the Maritime Domain", it ran for ten days across a harbour phase and a sea phase. India was the lead nation and South Africa the host.

India deployed INS Tarkash, a guided-missile stealth frigate with an integral Chetak helicopter. Brazil sent the corvette BNS Barroso, carrying a Lynx helicopter. The South African Navy fielded the frigate SAS Amatola, the inshore patrol vessels SAS King Sekhukhune I and SAS Adam Kok III, and the submarine SAS Manthatisi, with Gripen fighters of the South African Air Force in support.

Crews trained in surface, anti-air and anti-submarine warfare, as well as interdiction, anti-piracy operations and search and rescue. The harbour phase covered joint planning, lectures, communications training and cross-deck familiarisation. The drills let sailors exchange best practices and align procedures.

At the closing ceremony, the Commanding Officer of INS Tarkash said exercises like IBSAMAR turn long-standing diplomatic ties into practical naval cooperation. Official statements said the exercise reflects the three countries' shared commitment to safe, secure and open seas under a rules-based order.

IBSAMAR is the naval arm of the IBSA Dialogue Forum and has been held roughly every two years since 2008. The exercise aims to build interoperability among the three navies and help safeguard vital international shipping lanes.
